issues.title: Disable Delete Option for Shared Users in Sub-Organization Role Assignments
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

In sub-organizations, when viewing users assigned to a role, the delete option is available for all users, including shared users from the parent organization (with shared types `SHARED`, `INVITED`, or `OWNER`). However, it has been restricted to remove shared users of the types `SHARED` and `OWNER` from their assigned roles during the sharing process. Attempting to remove these shared users of the types `SHARED` or `OWNER` results in an error, creating a poor user experience. The UI does not proactively indicate which users cannot be removed, leading to confusion and unnecessary errors, which is bad UX.

### Suggested Improvement

Disable or remove the delete option for shared users in the sub-organizations role assignment view. This will:
1. Provide a clear visual indication that shared users of the types `SHARED` and `OWNER` cannot be removed from their assigned roles.
2. Prevent users from attempting actions that will result in errors.
3. Enhance the overall UX by making restrictions clear upfront.

### Version

7.1.0-beta

issues.title: Resubscribe to beacon subnets if current epoch dependent root changed
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

We have this function `handleAttesterDutiesReorg` which is mostly called when head (`onNewHead`) is updated
- and dependent root for next epoch changed
- or dependent root for current epoch changed

https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/1aa656191c84e3b55281bb8f21c9f4a529282500/packages/validator/src/services/attestationDuties.ts#L348

In both those cases we handle the reorg by
- getting updated attestater duties (`getAttesterDuties`)
- update cached duties (`dutiesByIndexByEpoch`)
- recalculate proof (`is_aggregator`)

But I noticed we are not resubscribing to beacon subnets (`prepareBeaconCommitteeSubnet`). This is not an issue if the dependent root for the next epoch changed as we re-/subscribe to current (_N_) and next epoch (_N+1_) at the start of each epoch.
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/1aa656191c84e3b55281bb8f21c9f4a529282500/packages/validator/src/services/attestationDuties.ts#L196

However, this is an issue if dependent root for current epoch changed as previous subscriptions are no longer valid
- validator duties changed (slot, committee index, etc.)
- `is_aggregator` results are different

### Expected behavior

Validators should be resubscribed to beacon committee subnets if current epoch dependent root changed.

Ideally, should just always resubscribe when `handleAttesterDutiesReorg` is called even if dependent root for next epoch changed as the subscriptions for epoch _N+1_ are outdated as well and the sooner we subscribe to subnets, the more likely it is to find good peers.

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux

### Lodestar version or commit hash

v1.11.3 / unstable (1aa656191c84e3b55281bb8f21c9f4a529282500)

### Describe problem solved by the proposed feature

主线目前最新已经支持并合并了clang-format机制，相比较之前的.ignore_format.yml机制，现在需要统一替换为.clang-format-ignore机制（clang-format原生支持的机制），该功能用于指定clang-format工具应该跳过哪些文件或目录的格式化

### Describe your preferred solution

需要完成两件事情：

1.在每个.ignore_format.yml位置，创建一个名为.clang-format-ignore文件，然后将其中的排除规则放到.clang-format-ignore文件中（注意语法规则）

2.将涉及到.ignore_format.yml文件机制的脚本统一修改为.clang-format-ignore机制，最终删除掉所有的.ignore_format.yml

* https://github.com/RT-Thread/rt-thread/blob/master/tools/ci/format_ignore.py
* https://github.com/RT-Thread/rt-thread/blob/master/tools/ci/file_check.py

下面是一个.clang-format-ignore文件的示例：
```
# .clang-format-ignore 文件功能说明：
# 1. 用于指定clang-format工具应该跳过哪些文件或目录的格式化
# 2. 采用类似.gitignore的语法规则
# 3. 支持通配符模式和路径匹配
# 4. 文件位置通常放在项目根目录，clang-format会递归应用这些规则

# =====================
# 核心语法规则示例
# =====================

# 规则1: 精确目录匹配 - 忽略指定目录下的所有内容
/build/

# 规则2: 通配符*匹配 - 忽略所有以".o"结尾的文件
*.o

# 规则3: 递归**匹配 - 忽略任意层级下的node_modules目录
**/node_modules/

# 规则4: 单字符?匹配 - 忽略类似".a", ".b"的单个字符扩展名
*.?

# 规则5: 字符集[]匹配 - 忽略".a"和".b"文件
*.[ab]

# 规则6: 模式组合 - 忽略src下所有子目录中的test文件夹
/src/**/test/

# 规则7: 相对路径模式 - 忽略当前目录下的临时文件
/tmp_*

# 规则8: 注释用法 - 以#开头的行会被视为注释
# 这是一个注释示例

# 规则9: 文件类型排除 - 忽略所有Markdown文档
**/*.md

# 规则10: 构建输出排除 - 忽略常见的构建输出目录
/out*/
/dist/
/target/

# 规则11: 第三方代码排除 - 忽略第三方依赖目录
/third_party/
/vendor/

# 规则12: 隐藏目录排除 - 忽略所有以点开头的目录

issues.title: [Feature][SQL function]  Enhance SQL Transform `substring`/`substr` functions to support date type fields
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [feature](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Feature%22) and found no similar feature requirement.


### Description

Currently, in SeaTunnel's SQL Transform, the `substring` and `substr` functions can only operate on string type fields. However, when trying to extract portions of a date or timestamp field (e.g., only getting the year part from a date), users have to explicitly convert the date field to string first, which is not intuitive and introduces extra complexity.

## Current Behavior

When trying to use `substring` function directly on a date field:

```sql
SELECT substring(update_time, 1, 10) FROM my_table
```

This fails because the `substring` function doesn't accept date/timestamp input types.

## Expected Behavior

The `substring` and `substr` functions should be able to automatically handle date/timestamp types by converting them to a standard string representation before performing the substring operation. For example:

```sql
-- Should return '2023-01-15' (just the date part)
SELECT substring(timestamp_column, 1, 10) FROM my_table 

-- Should return '2023' (just the year)
SELECT substring(date_column, 1, 4) FROM my_table
```
just like the Database, eg.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb059051-bc8e-4661-ba0f-90a6be8df187)

## Proposed Solution

Enhance the `StringFunction.substring()` method in the SQL Transform implementation to:

1. Check if the input is a date type (Date, Timestamp, LocalDate, LocalDateTime, etc.)
2. If it is, convert it to a string using a standardized formatter (e.g., `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` for timestamps)
3. Then perform the substring operation as usual


## Benefits

1. Improved user experience by allowing direct manipulation of date fields
2. Alignment with common SQL behavior in popular databases


## Affected Component

SQL Transform module in SeaTunnel transforms-v2.

issues.title: [Feature]: Add S3 Support for CO2 Footprint Report Output
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Thank you again for this plug-in!

### Summary
The `nf-co2footprint` plugin currently does not support writing CO2 footprint reports directly to S3 paths. When S3 URLs are specified in the `file` configuration parameters, the plugin appears to write to local filesystem instead of the specified S3 location.

### Current Behavior
When configuring the plugin with S3 paths:

```nextflow
co2summary {
    enabled = true
    file    = "s3://my-bucket/pipeline_info/co2footprint_summary_${trace_timestamp}.txt"
}
co2trace {
    enabled = true
    file    = "s3://my-bucket/pipeline_info/co2footprint_trace_${trace_timestamp}.txt"
}
co2report {
    enabled = true
    file    = "s3://my-bucket/pipeline_info/co2footprint_report_${trace_timestamp}.html"
}
```

The plugin generates files locally in the working directory instead of writing to the specified S3 paths.

### Expected Behavior
The plugin should support S3 paths and write CO2 footprint reports directly to the specified S3 locations, similar to how Nextflow's built-in reporting features (timeline, report, trace, dag) handle S3 paths when `params.outdir` is an S3 URL.

### Environment
- **Plugin Version**: 1.0.0
- **Nextflow Version**: 25.04.6
- **Cloud Platform**: AWS Batch
- **Storage**: S3

### Configuration Example
```nextflow
// In nextflow.config
plugins {
    id 'nf-co2footprint@1.0.0'
}

params {
    outdir = "s3://my-bucket/pipeline-results"
}

co2summary {
    enabled = true
    file    = "${params.outdir}/pipeline_info/co2footprint_summary_${trace_timestamp}.txt"
}
co2trace {
    enabled = true
    file    = "${params.outdir}/pipeline_info/co2footprint_trace_${trace_timestamp}.txt"
}
co2report {
    enabled = true
    file    = "${params.outdir}/pipeline_info/co2footprint_report_${trace_timestamp}.html"
}
```

This should write the CO2 footprint files directly to the S3 bucket at the specified paths.

### Use case(s):

This feature is essential for cloud-native pipelines where:
1. All pipeline outputs are stored in S3
2. Local filesystem storage is limited or temporary
3. CO2 footprint reports need to be archived alongside other pipeline artifacts

### Suggested implementation:

### Proposed Implementation
The plugin could leverage Nextflow's built-in file system abstraction (`FileHelper.asPath()`) to support S3 paths natively, similar to how other Nextflow features handle cloud storage.

### Workaround
Currently using a workaround that generates files locally and syncs to S3 in `workflow.onComplete`, but native S3 support would be more elegant and consistent with Nextflow's cloud-first approach.

issues.title: Add JsonToJsonl task
issues.body:
### Feature description

Too many users have to tediously do:

```yaml
  - id: json_to_ion
    type: io.kestra.plugin.serdes.json.JsonToIon
    from: "{{ outputs.download.uri }}"
    newLine: false # regular json

  - id: ion_to_jsonl
    type: io.kestra.plugin.serdes.json.IonToJson
    from: "{{ outputs.json_to_ion.uri }}"
    newLine: true # JSON-L
```

Only to get from the JSON returned by a typical API to a JSON-L format needed by kestra tasks such as e.g. `ForEachItem`.

**We should instead allow (without going through Ion):**

```yaml
  - id: json_to_jsonl
    type: io.kestra.plugin.serdes.json.JsonToJsonl
    from: "{{ outputs.download.uri }}"
```

full example showing the current state:

```yaml
id: iterate_over_json
namespace: company.team

tasks:
  - id: download
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.http.Download
    uri: "https://api.restful-api.dev/objects"
    contentType: application/json
    method: GET
    failOnEmptyResponse: true
    timeout: PT15S

  - id: json_to_ion
    type: io.kestra.plugin.serdes.json.JsonToIon
    from: "{{ outputs.download.uri }}"
    newLine: false # regular json

  - id: ion_to_jsonl
    type: io.kestra.plugin.serdes.json.IonToJson
    from: "{{ outputs.json_to_ion.uri }}"
    newLine: true # JSON-L

  - id: for_each_item
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.ForEachItem
    items: "{{ outputs.ion_to_jsonl.uri }}"
    batch:
      rows: 1
    namespace: company.team
    flowId: mysubflow
    wait: true
    transmitFailed: true
    inputs:
      json: "{{ json(read(taskrun.items)) }}"
```

issues.title: [Pituguês] Interpolação
issues.body:
## Em Python 
A interpolação é possível com a o método `f-strings` :
```python
name = 'World'
program = 'Python'
print(f'Hello {name}! This is {program}')
```
Ou seja, temos o prefixo `f` antes das aspas simples e quando indicarmos a variável/valor que deve ser interpolado no texto, o colocamos entre chaves `{ }`.

## Em Pituguês
No momento atual, o Pituguês herdou a mesma forma de interpolação que a linguagem Delégua, resultando nesta sintaxe:
```python
var minha_variavel = "Strogonoff"
imprima("Eu gosto de ${minha_variavel}") # Escreverá "Eu gosto de Strogonoff"
```

## Issue
Alterar a interpolação de Pituguês aproximando-a ao formato de Python, aceitando interpolação com variáveis ou operações.
Exemplo:
```python
# Inteporação com variável e texto
var minha_variavel = "Strogonoff"
imprima(f"Eu gosto de $minha_variavel}") 

# Interpolação com operação
imprima(f"O preço é { 2 * 8}")
```

* https://github.com/DesignLiquido/pitugues-docs/wiki/Estruturas-de-Dados-Elementares#interpola%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-texto

issues.title: BNF grammar should be whitespace-insensitive for epsilon productions
issues.body:
## Problem

The hand-coded BNF grammar in `lib/Chalk/Grammar/BNF.pm` is currently sensitive to trailing whitespace in epsilon productions. This causes parse failures for valid BNF syntax.

### Current Behavior

**Works**: `Rule ->\n` (no trailing whitespace)
**Fails**: `Rule -> \n` (trailing space before newline)

### Root Cause

The GrammarRule pattern uses `qr/\s*/` after `->`, which matches ALL whitespace including newlines:

```perl
['GrammarRule', [
    qr/[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*/,  # LHS
    qr/\s*/,                  # Optional whitespace
    '->',
    qr/\s*/,                  # ← This consumes the newline!
    'RHS'
]],
```

When trailing whitespace exists, the `qr/\s*/` matches both the space AND the newline, leaving nothing for the `Line` rule to match:

```perl
['Line', ['GrammarRule', "\n"]],  # ← No newline left to match
```

### Impact

- **Phase 7 Workaround**: Removed trailing whitespace from 4 epsilon productions in `grammar/perl.bnf` (lines 243, 288, 371, 462)
- **Future Risk**: Any BNF file with trailing whitespace will fail to parse

### Attempted Solution

Changing `qr/\s*/` to `qr/[ \t]*/` (horizontal whitespace only) was attempted but caused other parsing failures. The issue is more complex than a simple pattern change.

### Proposed Solutions

**Option 1**: Restructure GrammarRule pattern
- Use negative lookahead to prevent consuming newlines: `qr/(?:[^\S\n]*)/`
- May require adjusting other patterns that expect RHS to consume trailing whitespace

**Option 2**: Preprocess BNF content
- Strip trailing whitespace before parsing
- Simple but doesn't address root cause

**Option 3**: Restructure grammar rules
- Separate epsilon productions from normal productions
- `GrammarRule -> LHS '->' RHS | LHS '->' EpsilonMarker`
- More explicit but requires grammar redesign

### Recommendation

Start with Option 1 (pattern fix) with comprehensive testing. The core issue is that `qr/\s*/` is too greedy at the end of GrammarRule. We need a pattern that:
1. Matches horizontal whitespace after `->` 
2. Does NOT consume newlines
3. Works correctly for both epsilon and non-epsilon productions

### Test Case

```perl
# Should parse successfully with semantic actions
my $bnf = <<'BNF';
Rule1 -> 
Rule2 -> Element
Rule3 -> Element1 Element2
BNF

my $g = Chalk::BNF::parse_with_semantic_actions($bnf);
# Currently fails if Rule1 has trailing space
```

### Related Work

- Phase 7 completion: #63
- Semantic actions architecture: Feature branch `feature/semantic-actions-architecture`
- Working epsilon productions: Lines 197, 285, 371, 462 in perl.bnf (no trailing whitespace)

issues.title: Make waitAck Cache Configurable in StatusUpdaterBolt
issues.body:
Allow the waitAck cache in [StatusUpdaterBolt](https://github.com/apache/stormcrawler/blob/main/external/opensearch/src/main/java/org/apache/stormcrawler/opensearch/persistence/StatusUpdaterBolt.java#L163)  to be configured via a cache specification string (similar to how AbstractStatusUpdaterBolt handles its internal cache), instead of being hard-coded.

In the current implementation, waitAck is initialized as follows:

```
waitAck = Caffeine.newBuilder()
    .expireAfterWrite(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .removalListener(this)
    .build();
```

This configuration is static: both the expiration time and cache size are fixed. Users cannot adjust it through configuration. Under heavy indexing loads or high latency in OpenSearch responses, this can lead to:

- Premature eviction of pending tuples.
- “Purged from waitAck” errors in logs.
- Storm replaying tuples and OpenSearch returning 409 CONFLICT or 429 TOO MANY REQUESTS responses.

**Idea**:

Add a configuration parameter (e.g. `opensearch.status.updater.waitack.cache.spec`) that allows the cache to be built from a Caffeine specification string, just like the one used in `AbstractStatusUpdaterBolt`.

issues.title: Simplify dictionary encoding indices
issues.body:
The dictionary encoding process for fixed-width data always uses 32-bit dictionary indices.  This is good.  The process for variable-width data either uses 32-bit indices or 64-bit indices depending on the width of the variable-width offsets.  This doesn't really make sense.  We should just use 32-bit dictionary indices in all cases.  Alternatively, we could always use 64-bit indices.  That being said, I don't think we can have more than 2^32 values per disk page so 32-bit indices should be fine.  There is no need for anything smaller because dictionary indices should be getting bit-packed anyways.

If we standardize this then I think we can also make the size estimation step a little easier.

issues.title: Allow dictionary encoding to support more fixed width types
issues.body:
Currently the dictionary encoding in 2.1 only applies to some 128-bit fixed-width types.  I think this was a combination of a few things:

* At the time, we were not bit-packing indices, and so applying dictionary encoding to smaller types was unlikely to be beneficial
* Estimating cardinality on all columns was expensive
* TPC-H data has a lot of 128-bit decimals that benefit from dictionary encoding so there was an outsized (and unrealistic) benchmarking gain to focusing on 128-bit types.

However, we should at least be considering dictionary encoding for 64-bit types and maybe even 32-bit types.

issues.title: Website: Create an article summarizing the presentation "Documentation as code" done by Robert Kratky
issues.body:
# Goal
On the [Open Documentation Academy website](https://documentationacademy.org/), add an article containing both the video [ODH-015: Documentation as code](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AVNfH99KiME), done by Robert Kratky, and a concise summary of the video.

# Context
Some great presentations and discussions have occurred during CODA's Community Hour. Sadly, people may have little time or energy, and they might not listen to a 30-minute video even if the topic could interest them.

Reasons for making a concise summary of the video:
* Make the video’s information accessible to more people.
* Make the video’s information easy to skim through. Key information could be highlighted.
* For learning purposes, anyone can quickly review this summary at any time to refresh their knowledge.
* The video is available for anyone wanting to deep-dive into the topic. The article may invite more people to listen to it.

# Advices
## Where do you add your document in the Information Architecture of the website?
The document could be added to > Writing resources > Explanation. 

## Structure
Ideally, each article should follow the same structure. The first contributor can define a template to be followed by the other contributors.

My proposal: (feel free to improve it)
* Title (which is the same as the video for findability)
* Video
* Summary

## My own notes
**_Note: These are my personal notes for my own learning. They can absolutely be improved. Don’t hesitate to use them if you want to._**

### What does “Docs as code” mean?
Writing, testing, publishing, and maintaining documentation using the same tools developers use for software code.
Goals: content authoring (text editor), formatting (markup languages), version control (git) , issue tracking (JIRA), testing, validation, publishing, etc.

### Benefits for dev teams
* Dev can contribute or review easily the documentation
* They consider it a part of the project more easily 
* Documentation will be integrated in the product planning / in the definition of done
* Documentation is included in the project workflow
* Sense of common responsibility

### Benefits for organizations or projects
* Easy switch to different formats and tools
* Tighter collaboration between teams 
* Efficiency
* Aligning releases with publishing

### Challenges for technical authors and devs
* Can be challenging because there is a steep learning curve
* Resistance from devs, documentation slow down the “done”
* Corrections are more visible

## Transcription tool
You can listen to the video yourself and take notes, or you can also use a tool to transcribe the audio to text. I like this [transcription tool](https://ytb2mp4.com/youtube-transcript) but feel free to use any of the ones you like!

## Additional idea
Some very interesting topics are sometimes discussed during the time for questions that happens after the presentation. Feel free to include any questions and responses you think are useful.

issues.title: Online Stock Span (leetcode 901)
issues.body:
Hello there !!

The span of the stock's price in one day is the maximum number of consecutive days (starting from that day and going backward) for which the stock price was less than or equal to the price of that day.

For example, if the prices of the stock in the last four days is [7,2,1,2] and the price of the stock today is 2, then the span of today is 4 because starting from today, the price of the stock was less than or equal 2 for 4 consecutive days.
Also, if the prices of the stock in the last four days is [7,34,1,2] and the price of the stock today is 8, then the span of today is 3 because starting from today, the price of the stock was less than or equal 8 for 3 consecutive days.
Implement the StockSpanner class:

StockSpanner() Initializes the object of the class.
int next(int price) Returns the span of the stock's price given that today's price is price.
 

Example 1:

Input
["StockSpanner", "next", "next", "next", "next", "next", "next", "next"]
[[], [100], [80], [60], [70], [60], [75], [85]]
Output
[null, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 4, 6]

Explanation
StockSpanner stockSpanner = new StockSpanner();
stockSpanner.next(100); // return 1
stockSpanner.next(80);  // return 1
stockSpanner.next(60);  // return 1
stockSpanner.next(70);  // return 2
stockSpanner.next(60);  // return 1
stockSpanner.next(75);  // return 4, because the last 4 prices (including today's price of 75) were less than or equal to today's price.
stockSpanner.next(85);  // return 6

issues.title: briefcase create throws an exception on Gentoo ("Can't determine the system python version")
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm on Gentoo.
When I run the command "briefcase create", if fails with "Can't determine the system python version".

### Steps to reproduce

1. Follow the steps from the BeeWare tutorial, including
2. briefcase create

### Expected behavior

I expect that the command works without throwing an exception.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Environment

- Operating System: Gentoo
- Python version: 3.13.5
- Software versions:
  - Briefcase: 0.3.25
  - Toga: 0.5.2


### Logs

[briefcase.2025_09_26-17_14_29.create.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22565901/briefcase.2025_09_26-17_14_29.create.log)

```

```


### Additional context

Reason for throwing the exception:

The method "verify_system_python()" in system.py resolves the path `"/usr/bin/python3"` to `"/usr/bin/python-exec2c"`.

The value is then assigned to variable system_version, i.e.

`system_version == "/usr/bin/python-exec2c"`

Obviously the exception is thrown here:

```
if system_version[0] != "python3" or len(system_version) == 1:
  raise BriefcaseCommandError("Can't determine the system python version")

```
On Gentoo, /usr/bin/python3 is a symbolic link to python-exec2c which is a python wrapper
to be able to switch between multiple versions of Python installed at the same time.

issues.title: WorkerThread does not handle shell command output correctly (buffering and ordering issues)
issues.body:
There is a bug in how Peppy's WorkerThread handles output from shell commands, leading to two user-facing issues:

1. **Output Buffering**: For commands that produce output over time, the output is not displayed until the command finishes, making the application feel unresponsive.
2. **Incorrect Output Order**: For commands that write to both stdout and stderr, the messages may appear in the wrong order.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Bug 1: Output Buffering**

1. Launch Peppy.
2. Type the following command and press Enter:
```
/ { echo "START"; sleep 2; echo "END"; }
```
3. **Observed Behavior:** No output appears for 2 seconds, then "START" and "END" appear simultaneously.
4. **Expected Behavior:** "START" should appear immediately, followed by a 2-second pause, then "END".

---

**Bug 2: Incorrect Output Order**

1. Launch Peppy.
2. Type the following command and press Enter:
```
/ { echo "This should be first (stderr)" >&2; echo "This should be second (stdout)"; }
```
3. **Observed Behavior:** Output appears in the wrong order:

```
This should be second (stdout)
This should be first (stderr)
```

4. **Expected Behavior:** Output should appear in the order generated:
```
This should be first (stderr)
This should be second (stdout)
```

---

### Root Cause

The `run` method in `src/utils/command_worker.py` reads from stdout and stderr using blocking `readline()` calls sequentially. This prevents real-time display and can cause race conditions where output from one stream is processed before another, regardless of execution order.

---

issues.title: store.registerReducers
issues.body:
# store.registerReducers

The `store` has been updated with a new structure and additional features to more closely resemble how **Redux** works. Please note that you must **not** delete anything from `modules/store.js`; instead, you should **add** new functionality. This ensures forward compatibility, as older methods of using the store may be deprecated in future releases.

You should also create a new store constant. The name of this variable is up to you, but it should clearly represent the data it manages. The store should be defined as an **object** containing keys and values (with initial values).

Reducers should be stored separately from the state, but each reducer must be invoked to obtain the **initial state** for its corresponding key.

## What is a reducer?

A **reducer** is a function that takes an action object (`{ type, payload }`) and returns the new state for the appropriate key.

## Input

- `reducers`: an object following this format — `{ key: reducer }`  
  - Each `reducer` should be a callable function.

issues.title: Input Validation: Strengthen input validation and sanitization
issues.body:
## Problem

The webhook payload processing lacks proper input validation and sanitization:

1. **Unvalidated Data**: Raw payload data is processed without validation
2. **Injection Risks**: Unescaped data could lead to command injection in git operations
3. **Data Integrity**: No validation of required fields or data types
4. **Security Vulnerabilities**: Malicious payloads could exploit the system
5. **Error Handling**: Invalid data causes unclear error messages

## Current Issues

The webhook endpoint processes payload data directly without:
- Field validation (required vs optional)
- Data type checking
- Length limits
- Character sanitization
- URL validation for clone URLs

## Solution

Implement comprehensive input validation:

- **Field Validation**: Validate required fields and data types
- **Data Sanitization**: Sanitize strings and URLs before processing
- **Length Limits**: Prevent oversized payloads
- **URL Validation**: Validate clone URLs before git operations
- **Error Messages**: Provide clear validation error responses

## Success Criteria
- All webhook payloads validated before processing
- Clear error messages for invalid data
- Sanitized data used in all operations
- No direct use of raw payload data

issues.title: Charmed Ceph: Replace gerunds with imperatives
issues.body: > [! IMPORTANT] **Notice that this task contains a `workshop` label; this means that it has been created for the live DjangoCon/Ubucon 2025 Open Documentation Academy workshop to assist community members make their first documentation contribution. Please, do not work on this task unless it is assigned to you.** ## Background In the [Charmed Ceph how-to guides](https://ubuntu.com/ceph/docs/howtos), the use of gerund instead of imperative violates a our [style guide](https://docs.ubuntu.com/styleguide/en/). It also creates an inconsistent voice in both the index and text. The use of imperative delivers a clear command and helps users understand they need to perform an action. The use of gerund can hint at a description, and can lead to confusion, as users might think an explanation will follow. This reduces the precision of the documentation and reduces the functional quality. Since the information is not presented in the most actionable way, it can be harder to engage with and feel less intuitive to the user, which could decrease the deep quality. For example, “Replace OSD disks” rather than “Replacing OSD disks” is clearer that it is a step to be followed rather than an explanation, and, therefore, more actionable. ## Task Replace all gerunds in the index with imperatives, e.g. change “Installing Ceph” to “Install Ceph”. ## Resources - [Charmed Ceph docs](https://ubuntu.com/ceph/docs) - Follow our documentation contributing guide](https://canonical-microceph.readthedocs-hosted.com/latest/contributing/) - especially how to [edit docs on Discourse](https://ubuntu.com/ceph/docs/contribute-to-our-docs#p-149391-editing-on-discourse) - Read the [Ubuntu Code of Conduct](https://ubuntu.com/community/ethos/code-of-conduct). - [Visit the academy website](https://documentationacademy.org/) to learn more Thank you in advance for your contribution!

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Add node control protocol buffer and gRPC endpoints
issues.body:
## Describe the problem you'd like to have solved

Currently, there is no dedicated protocol buffer definition or gRPC endpoints for performing node control operations such as purging the transaction pool, retrieving memory usage, or querying node uptime. This limits the ability to programmatically manage and monitor node health and behavior, especially in production environments where such controls are crucial for automation and diagnostics.

### Describe the ideal solution

- Design and implement a new protocol buffer definition for node control operations.
- Add the following gRPC methods:
  - `PurgeTxPool`: Purges (clears) the node's transaction pool.
  - `GetMemoryInfo`: Returns memory information (free, used, total).
  - `GetUptime`: Returns the node's uptime duration.
- Integrate these methods in the node's gRPC server, guarded by a new configuration boolean `enable_control` within the `[grpc]` configuration section of `config.toml`. When enabled, the node should register and expose the control service.
- Update documentation and the example config (`example_config.toml`) to include the new `enable_control` option.

### Alternatives and current work-around

- Manual intervention for transaction pool purge or memory information retrieval through logs or command line, which is not programmatically accessible.
- Use of external monitoring tools, but without direct gRPC integration for control commands.

### Additional context

- Config section reference:

```toml
[grpc]
  enable = true
  enable_wallet = false
  # enable_control = false
```

- Example config file: [`config/example_config.toml`](https://github.com/aerium-network/aerium/blob/main/config/example_config.toml)
- The gRPC methods should only be registered if `enable_control` is set to `true` in the configuration.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Add Health check service
issues.body:
## Describe the problem you'd like to have solved

Currently, node APIs lack a standardized health check mechanism, making it hard to programmatically determine if the node is ready to serve requests or is in a healthy state. This can impact observability, automated monitoring, and orchestration in production environments.

### Describe the ideal solution

- Add support for health checking in node APIs by registering the gRPC health service using `grpc_health_v1.RegisterHealthServer(grpcServer, health.NewServer())`.
- Implement the health check service as defined in the [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/main/doc/health-checking.md).
- Use the official package [google.golang.org/grpc/health](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/health) to provide robust health status reporting.
- Ensure that clients can check both overall node health (using an empty service string) and per-service health if needed.

### Alternatives and current work-around

- Manual endpoint checks, less standardized and insufficient for gRPC-native integrations.
- No health reporting; external monitoring must rely on indirect checks (e.g., TCP port up).

### Additional context

- Reference: [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/main/doc/health-checking.md)
- Package: [google.golang.org/grpc/health](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/health)
- Example usage:

```go
import (
    "google.golang.org/grpc/health"
    grpc_health_v1 "google.golang.org/grpc/health/grpc_health_v1"
)

grpc_health_v1.RegisterHealthServer(grpcServer, health.NewServer())
```
- This will allow monitoring tools and orchestrators to query node health via standard gRPC APIs.

issues.title: Add a new trigger to detect stuck or misconfigured Schedule triggers
issues.body:
### Feature description

Add a new trigger that periodically checks for stuck or misconfigured Schedule triggers in Kestra. It can run at the tenant level, for a specific namespace, or for a single flow.

```yaml
id: detect_stuck_schedules
namespace: system

tasks:
  - id: send_alert
    runIf: "{{ trigger.data }}"
    type: io.kestra.plugin.notifications.slack.SlackIncomingWebhook
    url: https://kestra.io/api/mock
    messageText: The following Schedule triggers seem unhealthy {{ trigger.data }}

triggers:
  - id: stuck_schedules
    type: io.kestra.plugin.kestra.triggers.ScheduleMonitor
    auth:
      username: admin@kestra.io # pass your Kestra username as secret or KV pair
      password: Admin1234       # pass your Kestra password as secret or KV pair
    namespace: company.team     # optional, check a specific namespace
    flowId: daily_sync          # optional, check a specific flow
    interval: PT1H              # poll for stuck schedules every 1h
````

By default, the trigger should check all schedules in the current tenant if no namespace or flow is specified:

```yaml
triggers:
  - id: stuck_schedules
    type: io.kestra.plugin.kestra.triggers.ScheduleMonitor
    auth:
      username: admin@kestra.io # pass your Kestra username as secret or KV pair
      password: Admin1234       # pass your Kestra password as secret or KV pair
    interval: PT1H              # poll for stuck schedules every 1h
```

### Properties

| Property          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `auth`            | object  | Authentication credentials for Kestra API (username/password or API token, same as other existing tasks in the Kestra plugin). |
| `namespace`       | string  | Limit the check to a given namespace.                                                                                          |
| `flowId`          | string  | Limit the check to a specific flow.                                                                                            |
| `interval`        | string  | How often to poll for unhealthy scheduled triggers.                                                                            |
| `includeDisabled` | boolean | Whether to include disabled schedules in the check. Default: `false`.                                                          |

### Output

The trigger emits a list of schedules that appear stuck or misconfigured.

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "namespace": "company.team",
      "flowId": "daily_sync",
      "triggerId": "schedule",
      "lastExecution": "2025-10-13T06:00:00Z",
      "expectedNext": "2025-10-14T06:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Important for contributors

Make sure to use Kestra Java SDK here, as this has already been done on other tasks in this plugin.

issues.title: [BUG] DbZ-Exception in FireworkMode
issues.body:
### Version

_No response_

### What happened?

activation of FireworkMode always causes Divide-by-Zero-Exception.
Root Cause is line 71:
       ` Display.drawEllipse(rocketX, rocketY, radius, 1, true, UINT8_MAX / maxRadius * radius);`
when maxRadius is '0'. This may have two reasons:
1) value of `stage` has no initial value and may start with `stage = 2`. Solve by setting stage in `FireworkMode.h` at line 20:
stage = 0;

2) `maxRadius` is set by random at line 57 or 59. The range for random has no min value. Solve by setting `maxRadius` by
`maxRadius = random(**1**, min(COLUMNS`....

### Steps to Reproduce

invoke Mode "Fireworks"

### What did you expect to happen?

working without DbZ-Exception

### Which ESP32 board are you using?

_No response_

### Relevant Logs or Error Messages

```shell

```

### Any other helpful information?

I don't recommend initial mode by random (at `ModesService::ready()`, line 231:
`set(modules[random(0, modules.size())]->name);`
This may induce additional complexity in looking for root cause of restart reasons when this initial mode is faulty.
I would recommend setting a well known (and simple) mode as initial starting mode.

issues.title: [Discover][Traces] Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
issues.body:
**Kibana version:** 
9.1 and 8.19

**Describe the bug:**
Fatal error react detected under the obserbavility-traces-data-source-profile.

**Error:**

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
```

**Stack detail**
````
at F.traceItems (apm.chunk.9682.js:3:2363)
`````

**Likely Cause:**

* `traceItems` or data expected to be an array is `undefined`.

**Suggested Fix:**

* Guard `.map()` calls

issues.title: [NEW] Add solution for Counting Bits
issues.body:
## 🎯 Problem Information
- **Problem Name**: Counting Bits
- **CSES Link**: https://cses.fi/problemset/task/1146
- **Category**: Bitwise Operations
- **Estimated Difficulty**: [Medium]

## 📋 Problem Description
Your task is to count the number of one bits in the binary representations of integers between 1 and n.

## 💡 Proposed Approach
- Each bit position (0th, 1st, 2nd, ...) follows a repeating pattern:
    0 for 2^i numbers, then 1 for 2^i numbers.
- For each bit i:
    1. Count how many complete 0–1 cycles fit into 1..n.
    2. Add remaining 1s from the incomplete cycle.
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

issues.title: Consistently use compute ops in distance computations
issues.body:
Refactor the compute operations in our [distance primitives](https://github.com/intel/ScalableVectorSearch/tree/main/include/svs/core/distance).

The goal is that all `compute()` methods will dispatch to `simd::generic_simd_op()`, as it is done for example in

https://github.com/intel/ScalableVectorSearch/blob/18ba515e595ee65ff39d3abae3f42a56b3f5ab2c/include/svs/core/distance/euclidean.h#L321

To achieve this, the actual compute operation must be wrapped into a SIMD struct that provides the necessary protocol. One example is `L2FloatOp`

https://github.com/intel/ScalableVectorSearch/blob/18ba515e595ee65ff39d3abae3f42a56b3f5ab2c/include/svs/core/distance/euclidean.h#L240-L259

That is, it is necessary to provide `init()`, `accumulate()`, and `combine()` operations.

The chain `compute() -> simd::generic_simd_op() -> <actual compute>` is happening in many places already, but not consistently. One example where avx intrinsics are still used directly in `compute()` is

https://github.com/intel/ScalableVectorSearch/blob/18ba515e595ee65ff39d3abae3f42a56b3f5ab2c/include/svs/core/distance/euclidean.h#L369

But many other examples exist in our [distance primitives](https://github.com/intel/ScalableVectorSearch/tree/main/include/svs/core/distance).

issues.title: Add `TriggerRun` Task for Dagster Plugin
issues.body:
### Feature description

**Repository:** [kestra-io/plugin-dagster](http://github.com/kestra-io/plugin-dagster)

---

#### Summary

Create a new Kestra task `io.kestra.plugin.dagster.TriggerRun`, inspired by the existing [`TriggerDagRun` task from the Airflow plugin](https://kestra.io/plugins/plugin-airflow/io.kestra.plugin.airflow.dags.triggerdagrun#examples-body).  
This task should allow Kestra to trigger **Dagster job executions** (or asset materializations) through Dagster’s **GraphQL API**.

---

#### Context

While Airflow exposes a direct HTTP endpoint to trigger DAGs, Dagster relies on its **GraphQL API** (`/graphql`) to launch runs.  
Launching a run typically involves sending a GraphQL mutation (see [Dagster GraphQL docs](https://docs.dagster.io/api/graphql#launch-a-run)) that specifies:

- The **repository location** and **repository name**.
- The **job name** (or pipeline).
- An optional **run configuration** and **tags**.

This plugin would bridge Kestra and Dagster by allowing flows to programmatically start Dagster runs, poll their statuses, and retrieve results.

---

#### Example Usage

Trigger a Dagster job run with dynamic inputs and authentication:

```yaml
id: dagster
namespace: company.team

tasks:
  - id: run_dagster_job
    type: io.kestra.plugin.dagster.TriggerRun
    baseUrl: http://localhost:3000/graphql
    jobName: example_job
    repository: example_repo
    location: example_location
    wait: true
    pollFrequency: PT1S
    options:
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer {{ secret('DAGSTER_TOKEN') }}"
    body:
      runConfig:
        ops:
          example_op:
            config:
              param: "value"
      tags:
        source: kestra
        namespace: "{{ flow.namespace }}"
        flow: "{{ flow.id }}"
        task: "{{ task.id }}"
        execution: "{{ execution.id }}"
```

---

#### Implementation Notes

- Use **Dagster’s GraphQL `launchRun` mutation**:
  ```graphql
  mutation LaunchRun($executionParams: ExecutionParams!) {
    launchRun(executionParams: $executionParams) {
      __typename
      ... on LaunchRunSuccess {
        run {
          runId
          status
        }
      }
      ... on PythonError {
        message
        stack
      }
    }
  }
  ```
- Handle:
  - Custom headers (e.g., Bearer token, basic auth).
  - Polling until run completion (using Dagster’s `runStatus` queries).
  - Errors returned by GraphQL (especially `PythonError` responses).

---

#### References

- [Airflow `TriggerDagRun` Plugin](https://kestra.io/plugins/plugin-airflow/io.kestra.plugin.airflow.dags.triggerdagrun#examples-body)
- [Dagster GraphQL API Docs](https://docs.dagster.io/api/graphql)
- [Dagster Discussion: Triggering a Job via GraphQL](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/discussions/24246)
- [Dagster concepts](https://docs.dagster.io/getting-started/concepts)
- [Kestra Plugin Developer Guide](https://kestra.io/docs/plugin-developer-guide)

---

**Goal:** Provide first-class support for Dagster orchestration within Kestra by enabling job triggers and status tracking similar to Airflow’s integration. Please leave the Contributor Checklist and check it properly in your PR description 🙏

issues.title: Allow Qdrant to run on read-only FS
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently qdrant requires write access to storage directory, even if there are no write operations happening in the system.
It would be interesting in some scenarios to have an ability to run qdrant from read-only FS. For example, from the mounted network FS, so that multiple qdrant instances can serve same data.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Introduce a new CLI argument `--read-only` which will enable read only mode in qdrant.

For update APIs read-only instance should behave in the same way as for read-only API key - respond with `403 Forbidden` and explanation that the instance is in read-only mode.

Distributed deployment can't be read-only.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Automatic fallback into read-only if the file system doesn't allow writes, but it seems less flexible and error-prone.

**Additional context**

read-only mode assumes skipping WAL reading, so all changes should be applied and flushed to the real storage in advance


---

Note for contributors: Please consider this as tracking issue. If you think that it would be beneficial to split the task into multiple smaller PRs, please you are welcome to do so. Bounty will be rewarded for each PR independently

issues.title: feat: add spinner prop to Button and Loader components
issues.body:
### Description

Currently, the Button component uses a fixed internal Loader when isLoading is true. This limits flexibility since users cannot replace the loader with their own custom spinner.

To improve customization, the Button (and Loader) should expose a new prop:

``
spinner?: React.ReactNode
``

This allows consumers to pass a custom spinner element.
If no spinner is provided, it should fall back to the default Loader / Spinner used internally.

Location

 packages/snaps-ui/react/src/components/button/button.tsx

packages/snaps-ui/react/src/components/loader/index.tsx

## Proposed Solution

 1. Button Component
   - Add a new prop:
   ``
     spinner?: React.ReactNode
   ``
   - When isLoading is true:

      Render the passed spinner if provided, otherwise, fall back to the default <Loader />

2. Loader Component

   Also accept the same spinner?: React.ReactNode prop.

   If spinner is provided, render that instead of the internal <Spinner />.

Example:
   ``
     <Loader spinner={<CustomSpinner />} />
   ``

Example Usage

``
<Button
  isLoading
  spinner={<MyCustomSpinner color="red" />}
>
  Saving...
</Button>
``

Default Behavior (no spinner passed):

``
<Button isLoading>Saving...</Button>
``
uses inernal <Loader /> with <Spinner /> fallback.

issues.title: [FR] Display all AI SDK LLM message in pretty mode
issues.body:
Similar to #3413

**Context:**

Reading traces and span inputs is complicated especially when you have a lot of LLM messages in either the input or output of a traces and span.

The current Pretty mode [implementation](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/blob/804082382a83cf92044afe29040d6ba946d1fc47/apps/opik-frontend/src/lib/traces.ts#L40) checks the input / output fields for a messages array which follows a specific format and then we render the last message. We can improve this implementation as part of this work.

**Implementation**

Instead of displaying just the last message, we will display all LLM message in pretty mode. In order to achieve this, we should parse the messages array and display a collapsible section for each message. The title of each section will be the message type and the body will be the message content.

By default each section will be expanded apart from tool calls and tool call results.

The RFC 5545 describes all the properties we have in icalendar.prop.

Please add a `__doc__` string documentation for all of them.

Examples:

- [vMonth](https://icalendar.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#icalendar.prop.vMonth)

```python
class vGeo:
    """Geographic Position

    Property Name:  GEO

    Purpose:  This property specifies information related to the global
        position for the activity specified by a calendar component.

    Value Type:  FLOAT.  The value MUST be two SEMICOLON-separated FLOAT
        values.

    Property Parameters:  IANA and non-standard property parameters can
        be specified on this property.

    Conformance:  This property can be specified in "VEVENT" or "VTODO"
        calendar components.

    Description:  This property value specifies latitude and longitude,
        in that order (i.e., "LAT LON" ordering).  The longitude
        represents the location east or west of the prime meridian as a
        positive or negative real number, respectively.  The longitude and
        latitude values MAY be specified up to six decimal places, which
        will allow for accuracy to within one meter of geographical
        position.  Receiving applications MUST accept values of this
        precision and MAY truncate values of greater precision.

    Example:
        GEO:37.386013;-122.082932

        >>> geo = vGeo.from_ical('37.386013;-122.082932')
        >>> geo.latitude
        37.386013
        >>> geo.longitude
        -122.082932
    """
```

issues.title: Understanding how EF Core Cosmos DB Provider Works
issues.body:
# Task: NoSQL and Cosmos DB Review, Optimization, and Refactor Analysis

## Description
This task focuses on understanding and optimizing the current usage of **Azure Cosmos DB** within the project, identifying potential performance bottlenecks, and ensuring that data access patterns and SDK usage align with best practices.  
The goal is to evaluate whether Entity Framework Core (EF Core) or direct SDK usage provides better performance and maintainability in the existing architecture.

---

## Scope of Work

### 1. Codebase Revision and Refactor Assessment
- Review the existing data access and repository code related to Cosmos DB.  
- Identify sections that could benefit from refactoring to improve clarity, efficiency, or maintainability.  
- Evaluate whether the current EF Core integration introduces unnecessary abstraction or overhead.

### 2. Understanding NoSQL Concepts
- Study and document the fundamental principles of **NoSQL databases**, including document-based data modeling and partitioning strategies.  
- Assess how these concepts are currently reflected (or not) in the existing database schema and queries.

### 3. Cosmos DB SDK Evaluation
- Investigate the capabilities and limitations of the **Azure Cosmos DB SDK** compared to the EF Core provider.  
- Identify possible performance issues or overhead introduced by using EF Core over the native SDK.  
- Determine where each approach (EF Core vs SDK) is most suitable depending on project requirements.

### 4. Query Optimization and RU Cost Reduction
- Analyze current queries for efficiency and performance impact.  
- Optimize queries, indexing, and partition strategies to minimize **Request Units (RU)** consumption.  
- Explore caching or batching techniques to further reduce RU costs.

### 5. RU (Request Unit) Analysis
- Review how **Request Units (RU)** work in Azure Cosmos DB and how they are consumed by read, write, and query operations.  
- Document findings and provide recommendations for optimizing RU allocation and usage.

---

## Deliverables
- Detailed analysis of the current Cosmos DB implementation and data access layer  
- Recommendations for using either EF Core or the Cosmos SDK depending on use case  
- Optimized query patterns and partitioning strategy  
- Documentation on RU usage, cost factors, and best practices for performance optimization  
- Optional: Refactored data access components reflecting the proposed improvements  

---

## Goal
Ensure that the project leverages Azure Cosmos DB efficiently, minimizing operational costs while maintaining scalability, performance, and clean architectural principles.

issues.title: Handle missing `/etc/sudoers` with grace
issues.body:
**Describe the feature you'd like see implemented in `sudo-rs`**
If `/etc/sudoers` is missing, give a better error message than "file not found".

***or***

do something else that can be appropriate: interpret a missing `sudoers` file as:

1. All settings have their default value (like an empty sudoers file)
2. There is the implicit rule, which does what people naively expect sudo to do: grant escalationg privileges to people in the `sudoers` group.

**What problem can be solved with this feature?**
Users can end up in this situation by the present state of some packaging, or if they install our tarballs on a clean sudo-less system without creating a /etc/sudoers.

**Additional context**
I don't think the situation where a missing `/etc/sudoers` is interpreted as `%sudoersALL=ALL` diminishes security: the `/etc/sudoers` file is considered part of the trusted config...

issues.title: Feature Request: Text extraction from image posts
issues.body:
## Description:
Currently, there is no scanning procedure in place for image-based posts. The app should incorporate a model that can infer the presence of personal information in images with decent accuracy and low inference time.

## Possible Implementations:
1. Model converted to TFLite: Use an OCR model (like Tesseract or a lightweight CNN-based text detector) converted to TensorFlow Lite, embedded within the app, to extract text from images. Then analyze the text using the existing text post scanning pipeline.

2. Flutter OCR Packages: Integrate an existing Flutter package (e.g., google_ml_kit or firebase_ml_vision) to perform on-device OCR and extract text from images. Then pass extracted text through the same inference pipeline.

3. Backend-hosted Detection Model: Host a custom model in a secure backend to handle scanning, reducing app size and keeping the model private.

## Description:
Currently, users can only scan posts individually. In real-world platforms, posts often contain multiple images and text grouped together, and users need an aggregated risk assessment for the entire set.

## Proposed Solution:

issues.title: Feature Request: Add/Edit Metadata for Image Posts
issues.body:
## Description:
Currently, users can only upload single images. Adding the ability to include a custom caption or short description will help users add context, making images easier to organize and search later, also mimicking how posts are made in real life on different platforms. This leads to an overall better experience when scanning before posting.

## Proposed Solution:
 - Provide a text field when uploading or editing an image to add/edit captions or descriptions.
 - Encrypt and store metadata along with the image.
 - Use this metadata in search and sorting functionalities, and also add functionality to scan the metadata using the `TFLite model` for inferences in a similar way to text posts.

issues.title: Feature Request: Edit and Search Functions for Text Posts

 - Display matching posts in real-time or as a filtered list.
 - When an post is selected add an additional option along with scanning and deleting the post for editing its content only for text posts.

issues.title: [CodeStyle][Typos] ✏️ Typos 工具引入
issues.body:
## 背景 (Background)

为了进一步提升 PaddlePaddle 官方文档的专业性和准确性，我们计划引入自动化拼写检查工具 typos。文档中的拼写错误会影响用户的阅读体验，甚至可能导致对技术细节的误解。引入自动化检查工具可以在代码合并前发现并修复这些问题，是保障文档质量的有效手段。

### 对齐主仓库实践 (Alignment with Main Repository)

typos 工具已经在 Paddle 主仓库中成功引入并得到了良好实践，有效保障了代码注释和文档字符串的质量。这证明了该工具的价值和可行性。
相关的实践和讨论可以参考下面几个 issue：
- https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/Paddle/issues/69377
- https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/Paddle/issues/69441
- https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/Paddle/issues/69442
- https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/Paddle/issues/69483

在 docs 仓库中引入 typos，是我们将代码质量保障的最佳实践扩展到文档生态、保持项目整体一致性的重要一步。

### 任务目标 (Task Goals)
引入配置文件：在 docs 仓库根目录添加 typos 的配置文件 (_typos.toml)。需要根据文档的特性和常用术语，定制化词典，避免误报。
集成至 pre-commit 和 CI 中：确保所有新的 Pull Request 在合并前都会经过拼写检查，并且本地 commit 的时候就可发现 typo。
修复存量问题：在引入配置文件时，会给所有认为是 typo 单词都加入定制化词典，我们需要确认是否为 typo，对于 typo 我们需要手动修改它们

issues.title: [Bug]  Compatibility Issue with Node 24
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### Apache SkyWalking Component

License Tools (apache/skywalking-eyes)

### What happened



I encountered a significant issue while trying to run the `make license-dep` command in the banyandb project with Node.js version 24. It appears that the Skywalking eye does not function correctly with this version, resulting in license identification failures.

issues.title: 📚 문서 사이트 디자인 개선 - 가독성 및 사용성 향상
issues.body:
# 📚 문서 사이트 디자인 개선

## 🎯 목표
문서 사이트(`/app/docs`)의 가독성과 사용성을 개선하여 사용자가 쉽게 정보를 파악할 수 있도록 합니다.

## 📋 현재 문제점

### 1. **타이포그래피 & 콘텐츠 스타일**
- ❌ h2 요소에 `borderBottomColor: "gray.100"` 하드코딩 → 다크모드에서 거의 보이지 않음
- ❌ 링크가 `textStyle: "label1"` (14px bold) → 본문(16px)보다 작고 굵어서 부자연스러움
- ❌ 텍스트 여백이 좁아 답답함 (p 태그 상하 여백 8px만)
- ❌ h1에 여백 없음
- ❌ ul, ol, blockquote, code(인라인), hr 스타일이 정의되지 않음

### 2. **사이드바 (Aside)**
- ❌ 활성 항목 구분이 약함 (`primary/10` 배경만)
- ❌ 섹션 제목과 네비게이션 항목 구분이 불명확
- ❌ 모바일에서 완전히 숨김 (UX 문제)
- ❌ 기본 스크롤바 스타일

### 3. **코드 블록 (CodeBlock)**
- ❌ 복사 버튼 색상 `color: "black"` 하드코딩 → 다크모드에서 안 보임
- ❌ 코드 블록 컨테이너에 배경/테두리 없음
- ❌ 파일명이나 언어 표시 없음

### 4. **헤더 (Header)**
- ❌ 배경이 투명 → 스크롤 시 콘텐츠와 겹침
- ❌ 네비게이션 항목에 활성 상태 표시 없음

### 5. **콘텐츠 레이아웃**
- ❌ 콘텐츠 영역에 max-width 없음 → 넓은 화면에서 가독성 저하 (한 줄이 너무 길어짐)
- ❌ 여백 부족

---

## ✅ 개선 계획

### Phase 1: 핵심 가독성 개선 (필수)

#### 1.1. MDX 컴포넌트 스타일 개선
**파일**: `src/mdx-components.tsx`

**변경 사항**:
- **h1**: 상단 여백 추가 (mt: 8, mb: 4), `color: "foreground"` 추가
- **h2**: `borderBottomColor: "gray.100"` → `border: "base"` (시맨틱 토큰), 여백 증가 (mt: 12, mb: 4)
- **h3**: 여백 증가 (mt: 8, mb: 3)
- **p**: 여백 증가 (mt: 4, mb: 4), `lineHeight: "1.8"` 추가
- **a**: `textStyle: "label1"` → `textStyle: "body1"`, `color: "primary"`, 호버 효과 개선
- **ul, ol**: 리스트 스타일 추가 (들여쓰기, 마커, 항목 간격)
- **blockquote**: 인용구 스타일 추가 (좌측 primary border, muted 배경)
- **code**: 인라인 코드 스타일 추가 (muted 배경, rounded, monospace 폰트)
- **hr**: 구분선 스타일 개선 (시맨틱 border, 상하 여백 증가)

**예상 코드**:
```typescript
h2: (props) => (
  <h2 className={css({
    textStyle: "title2",
    mt: "12",
    mb: "4",
    borderBottom: "base",  // ✅ 시맨틱 토큰
    pb: "3",
    color: "foreground",
  })} {...props} />
),

a: (props) => (
  <a className={css({
    textStyle: "body1",    // ✅ 본문과 같은 크기
    color: "primary",      // ✅ primary 컬러
    textDecoration: "underline",
    textUnderlineOffset: "2px",
    _hover: { color: "primary/80" },
  })} {...props} />
),

ul: (props) => (
  <ul className={css({
    mt: "4",
    mb: "4",
    ml: "6",
    listStyleType: "disc",
    "& li": { mt: "2", mb: "2", pl: "2" },
  })} {...props} />
)
```

---

#### 1.2. 코드 블록 개선
**파일**: `src/components/codeBlock/index.tsx`

**변경 사항**:
- 복사 버튼 색상: `color: "black"` → 시맨틱 컬러 사용
- 버튼 배경: 반투명 배경 추가 (`bg: "muted/80"`)
- 코드 블록 컨테이너: `bg: "muted"`, `border: "base"`, `rounded: "lg"` 추가
- 내부 padding 조정

---

#### 1.3. 콘텐츠 레이아웃 개선
**파일**: `src/app/docs/layout.tsx`

**변경 사항**:
- `<styled.main>` 에 max-width 추가:
  ```typescript
  <styled.main 
    width="100%" 
    maxW="48rem"     // ✅ 768px 최대 너비
    mx="auto"        // ✅ 중앙 정렬
    px="6"           // 좌우 padding 증가
    py="8"           // 상하 padding 추가
    pos="relative"
  >
  ```

---

### Phase 2: 네비게이션 & 구조 개선 (중요)

#### 2.1. 사이드바 스타일 개선
**파일**: `src/components/aside/recipe.ts`

**변경 사항**:
- 활성 항목: 좌측 border accent 추가
  ```typescript
  navItem: {
    _before: {
      content: '""',
      position: "absolute",
      left: 0,
      top: "50%",
      transform: "translateY(-50%)",
      w: "3px",
      h: "60%",
      bg: "transparent",
      rounded: "full",
      transition: "all",
    }
  },
  variants: {
    active: {
      true: {
        navItem: {
          bg: "primary/10",
          color: "primary",
          fontWeight: "medium",
          _before: { bg: "primary" },  // ✅ 좌측 accent
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```
- 섹션 제목: `textStyle: "label1"` 적용, 상단 여백 증가
- 스크롤바 커스텀 스타일링

---

#### 2.2. 헤더 개선
**파일**: `src/components/header.tsx`

**변경 사항**:
- 반투명 배경 + backdrop blur:
  ```typescript
  <header className={flex({
    bg: "background/80",         // ✅ 반투명
    backdropFilter: "blur(8px)", // ✅ blur 효과
    borderBottom: "base",        // ✅ 하단 보더
    // ... 기존 스타일
  })}>
  ```
- 활성 링크 표시 (현재 페이지 하이라이트)

---

#### 2.3. 전역 스타일 개선
**파일**: `src/app/globals.css`

**추가 사항**:
```css
html {
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
}

::selection {
  background-color: var(--colors-primary);
  color: var(--colors-primary-foreground);
}

*:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--colors-primary);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

---

### Phase 3: 추가 컴포넌트 (선택적)

#### 3.1. Callout / Alert 컴포넌트
정보, 경고, 팁 등을 표시하는 컴포넌트
```tsx
<Callout type="info">
  이 컴포넌트는 Radix UI를 사용합니다.
</Callout>
```

#### 3.2. PropsTable 컴포넌트
Props 문서화 테이블
```tsx
<PropsTable>
  <PropRow name="variant" type="string" default="default" />
</PropsTable>
```

#### 3.3. ComponentPreview 컴포넌트
라이브 프리뷰 + 코드 표시
```tsx
<ComponentPreview>
  <Button>Example</Button>
</ComponentPreview>
```

---

## 📊 Before / After 비교

| 요소 | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| **h2 보더** | `gray.100` (다크모드 ❌) | `border: "base"` (다크모드 ✅) |
| **링크 크기** | 14px bold | 16px normal (본문과 같음) |
| **링크 색상** | 기본색 + opacity | `primary` 컬러 |
| **p 여백** | 8px 위아래 | 16px 위아래 |
| **h1 여백** | 없음 | 상단 32px, 하단 16px |
| **리스트** | 스타일 없음 | 들여쓰기 + 마커 |
| **인용구** | 없음 | 좌측 border + 배경 |
| **인라인 코드** | 없음 | muted 배경 + rounded |
| **콘텐츠 너비** | 제한 없음 | 최대 768px |
| **코드 복사 버튼** | 다크모드 안 보임 | 시맨틱 컬러 |
| **헤더 배경** | 투명 | 반투명 + blur |

---

## 🎯 기대 효과

✅ **다크모드 완벽 대응** - 모든 컬러가 시맨틱 토큰 사용  
✅ **가독성 대폭 향상** - 여백, 줄간격, 너비 최적화  
✅ **시각적 계층 명확** - 제목/본문/링크 구분이 뚜렷  
✅ **완성도 향상** - 누락된 요소들(리스트, 인용구, 인라인 코드) 추가  
✅ **UX 개선** - 헤더 고정, 사이드바 활성 표시, 코드 복사 버튼 개선  

---

## 📌 우선순위

**High Priority (즉시 필요)**:

---

## 🔗 관련 파일

- `app/docs/src/mdx-components.tsx` - MDX 요소 스타일
- `app/docs/src/components/codeBlock/index.tsx` - 코드 블록
- `app/docs/src/app/docs/layout.tsx` - 문서 레이아웃

issues.title: flake-stats: add number of merged PRs per day to box
issues.body:
<!-- Make sure that you visit our User Guide at https://kubevirt.io/user-guide.
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe**:
The flake-stats report[1] is our main tool to look at flaky tests during the SIG-CI meetings currently. It's been proven extremely useful to get a quick overview about where things go wrong. This is achieved by the overviews that aggregate failures per day and per lane.

Now, sometimes it seems that there are a lot of failures that have occurred on one day, solely being caused by the fact that a lot of PRs have been merged on that day - reason of this is that the sum of failures per day is taken from the flakefinder report which aggregates all the failures of a merged PR towards the day it was merged, and not towards the day the failure itself occurred.

> [!NOTE]
> **Example:** a PR that was created on Dec 21st and is merged on Jan 1st, during that period it's test lanes had been run several times, and there were some unit test failures on those runs. Now, all the failures are accounted towards the day the PR is getting merged, so that exactly that day looks as if a lot of failures occurred at that day - which again is not the case.

**Describe the solution you'd like**:
By adding the number of merged PRs to a day's numbers we can better spot anomalies - i.e. a high number of test failures even though the number of merged PRs is low might indicate that a flaky or unstable test got introduced.

Thus we want to show the number of PRs that have been merged on the day - added to the box that shows the failures for that day. Sketch:

| Mon, 26 Aug 2024 | |
| ---------------- | ----- |
| Failures | 42 |
| PRs merged | 10 |

**Additional context**:
* flake-stats code: https://github.com/kubevirt/project-infra/tree/main/robots/cmd/flake-stats
* flake-stats Go Template location: https://github.com/kubevirt/project-infra/blob/a609d2f66961a57e6a447e29151f44bf6cf14464/robots/cmd/flake-stats/flake-stats.gohtml#L32
* The number of PRs (also the actual PR numbers) is available from the json element "prNumbers"

[1]: https://storage.googleapis.com/kubevirt-prow/reports/flakefinder/kubevirt/kubevirt/flake-stats-14days.html

issues.title: Units larger than `h` in `GrafanaAlertRuleGroup#.spec.rules[*].for` are rejected on apply
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When exporting Alerts and AlertGroups from Grafana in order to populate a `GrafanaAlertRuleGroup` CR, we see that when specific values are picked for pending period( `.spec.rules[*].for`) like `24h`, Grafana will export it as `1d`.
At the time of writing, years, weeks, and days are not supported in the `.spec.rules[*].for` field.

**Version**
v5.19.4

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Open a Grafana `v11.5.3` or later
2. Create or modify an alert rule
3. Set the pending period to `24h`
4. Save and Export the alert, notice it should have converted the pending period to `1d`
5. Apply the rule as a CRD
6. ```
    # grafanaalertrulegroups.grafana.integreatly.org "grafana-health" was not valid:
    # * spec.rules[0].for: Invalid value: "1d": spec.rules[0].for in body should match '^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$'
    ```

**Expected behavior**
Following the above steps, the CRD should be succesfully applied and synchronized with matching instances.

**Suspect component/Location where the bug might be occurring**
https://github.com/grafana/grafana-operator/blob/44b51c8f2643ab00a76d609858419dbbe0ba422a/api/v1beta1/grafanaalertrulegroup_types.go#L52

**Runtime (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Linux
- Grafana Operator Version: v5.19.4
- Environment: Kubernetes 1.31
- Deployment type: Helm
- Other: N/A

**Additional context**
It might be worth it to remove `ns, us, µs, ms` as they do not make much sense as alert delays and add `d` and `w`. and omit `y` as that does not make much sense either.

issues.title: HibernateOrmProcessor causes Warning that package cannot be indexed due to package-info.java
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

If I want to define a global Hibernate **@FilterDef** the best practive way is to use a **package-info.java** next to the entities.

But this package-info.java during tests causes a WARN:

`2025-10-15 10:38:52,125 WARN  [io.qua.dep.ind.IndexWrapper] (build-26) Failed to index org.acme: Class does not exist in ClassLoader QuarkusClassLoader:Deployment Class Loader: TEST for JUnitQuarkusTest-no-profile (QuarkusTest)@7446d8d5`


_HibernateOrmProcessor.generateProxies_ calls the _IndexWrapper.getClassByName_ with the packageName and not an actual className as expected this causes the mentioned warn.

Everything seems to work fine expect the warning so, it probably would be enough to somewhere in HibernateORMProcessor filter out packages from the list of classes.

### Expected behavior

Test should run without producing an WARN message each time.

### Actual behavior

`2025-10-15 10:38:52,125 WARN  [io.qua.dep.ind.IndexWrapper] (build-26) Failed to index org.acme: Class does not exist in ClassLoader QuarkusClassLoader:Deployment Class Loader: TEST for JUnitQuarkusTest-no-profile (QuarkusTest)@7446d8d5`

Message is shown during test runs if package-info.java is present with hibernate @FilderDef inside.

### How to Reproduce?

[code-with-quarkus.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22922776/code-with-quarkus.zip)

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

_No response_

### Output of `java -version`

issues.title: Add optional `decommission_year` column to `assets.csv` input file
issues.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 -->
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Currently, at the very start of the simulation, we look through the assets defined in `assets.csv` and decommission any that _should_ have already been decommissioned according to their commission year and the expected lifetime of the process. For example, if the user defines an asset with a commission year of 1980, for a process with a lifetime of 30 year, and the simulation starts in 2020, then this asset will be decommissioned straight away and won't contribute to the dispatch optimisation in the first year. If this brings supply below demand for that year, then the model will fail. (Remember, MUSE doesn't perform any new investments in the first year, so can't make up for any shortfalls in this year).

The problem is that it's very possible (probably very common) for assets to outlive their prescribed lifetime. The very fact that an asset is included in the input file suggests that it probably _is_ still active, regardless of what the "expected" lifetime of the process is (although there may be exceptions to this, e.g. if the source data contains historical assets).

Whilst we don't necessarily want assets _installed by MUSE_ to outlive their expected lifetime, we need to allow this for existing assets, so that existing asset pools can be properly represented. Currently, the only way to signify that an old asset is still active is to either fudge the `commission_year` of the asset or the `lifetime` of the process, neither of which is very satisfying.

## Describe the solution you'd like

An optional `decommission_year` column in the `assets.csv` input file. If this is set, it can override the default decommission year for the asset (= `commission_year + lifetime`). If it's empty, the default commission year still applies.

In the above example, the user could put a decommission year of 2030 to signify that this asset is still active.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

We previously didn't have this problem because we didn't decommission any assets until after the first year's dispatch run. The implicit assumption was that any asset defined in `assets.csv` was still active in the first year, regardless of its expected lifetime. We could consider going back to this approach. The issue with this was that you could still get a "mass-decommissioning" event in the second year, which isn't very realistic.

Another idea, suggested by @martinstringer, would be to give process lifetimes a standard deviation, and perform decommissioning stochastically. Each year you would calculate "given that this asset has lasted this long, what's the probability that it gets decommissioned in this year". With this approach you would assume that any assets defined in `assets.csv` _do_ still exist, and therefore won't be decommissioned before the first dispatch run, but any assets beyond their expected lifetime would likely be decommissioned soon after. I'm well aware that introducing randomness to the model might have big implications, and may go against the spirit of MUSE. I think it's a good idea though.

## Additional context

This is relevant for the [UK power sector model](https://github.com/EnergySystemsModellingLab/MUSE_UK_power/tree/main/MUSE2_input_files), where a lot of the existing assets are well beyond their expected lifetimes

issues.title: [assemble] APP_HOME (java-archive) does not work if bin/app is linked in a relative way
issues.body:
### Task List

- [X] Steps to reproduce provided
- [ ] Stacktrace (if present) provided
- [X] Example that reproduces the problem (link to git repository is ideal)
- [X] Full description of the issue provided (see below)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Build an assembly
2. Extract app somewhere, e.g. `~/.local/apps/myapp/bin/myapp`
3. Link somewhere in a relative way, e.g. `(cd ~/.local/bin && ln -s ../apps/myapp/bin/app)`

### Expected Behaviour

When executed, should work

### Actual Behaviour

When executed, lib path is determined in a wrong way, because APP_HOME is not correctly resolved:

```
$ bash -x myapp
+ app_path=myapp
+ APP_HOME=
+ '[' -h myapp ']'
++ cd ./..
++ pwd -P
+ APP_HOME=/Users
```

... which is wrong.

### Workaround

Link in an absolute path: `(cd ~/.local/bin && ln -s ~/.local/apps/myapp/bin/app)`

Then:

```
$ bash -x ./myapp
+ app_path=./myapp
+ APP_HOME=./
+ '[' -h ./myapp ']'
++ ls -ld ./myapp
+ ls='lrwxr-xr-x  1 theUser  1000  57 17 Oct 10:47 ./myapp -> /Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/myapp'
+ link=/Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/myapp
+ case $link in
+ app_path=/Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/myapp
+ APP_HOME=/Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/
+ '[' -h /Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/myapp ']'
++ cd /Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT/bin/..
++ pwd -P
+ APP_HOME=/Users/theUser/.local/apps/myapp-1.2.0-SNAPSHOT
```


### Environment Information

- **Operating System**: MacOS
- **JReleaser Version:** latest/any
- **JDK Version:** any, not relevant for this issue (but I used IBM Semeru 17 and 25)

issues.title: Add SharePoint Sub-Plugin for Microsoft 365
issues.body:
### Feature description

### 📌 Context / Motivation  
The [Microsoft 365 plugin](https://github.com/kestra-io/plugin-microsoft365) is currently empty and does not yet provide service integrations.  
SharePoint is a critical service for many organizations, providing collaboration, file/document management, and intranet features.  

Adding a sub-plugin `io.kestra.plugin.microsoft365.sharepoint` will allow Kestra workflows to directly interact with SharePoint files and sites, aligned with the existing Drive/OneShare integration.

### 🎯 Proposal  
Introduce a new **SharePoint sub-plugin** with the same core tasks as the Google Drive and OneShare plugins, to ensure consistency:

#### Tasks  
1. **Create**  
   - Create a new file or folder in a SharePoint document library.  
   - API: `PUT /sites/{site-id}/drives/{drive-id}/items/{parent-id}:/{filename}:/content`  

2. **Delete**  
   - Delete a file or folder.  
   - API: `DELETE /sites/{site-id}/drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}`  

3. **Download**  
   - Download the content of a file.  
   - API: `GET /sites/{site-id}/drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}/content`  

4. **Export**  
   - Export a file to another format (e.g., Office document → PDF).  
   - API: `GET /sites/{site-id}/drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}/content?format={format}`  

5. **List**  
   - List items in a document library or folder.  
   - API: `GET /sites/{site-id}/drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}/children`  

6. **Upload**  
   - Upload a file (simple <4MB or chunked for larger files).  
   - API: `PUT /content` or `createUploadSession`  

#### Future Triggers (optional, next iteration)  
- **FileCreated**: react when a new file is created in a SharePoint library.  
- **FileUpdated**: react when a file is modified.  
  _(similar to OneShare, based on Microsoft Graph `subscription` API)_  

### 🔍 Requirements & Considerations  

| Aspect | Description |
|---|---|
| **SDK choice** | Use [Microsoft Graph SDK for Java](https://github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-java) |
| **Authentication** | OAuth2 client credentials / delegated auth via Azure AD |
| **Permissions** | Requires `Sites.Read.All`, `Sites.ReadWrite.All`, `Files.Read`, `Files.ReadWrite` |
| **Consistency** | Tasks must align with Google Drive and OneShare sub-plugins |
| **Error handling** | Handle permissions issues, large files, expired tokens |
| **Testing** | Unit tests with mocked Graph API + integration tests on a demo SharePoint site |
| **Documentation** | Provide YAML workflow examples for each task |

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria  

1. A new package `io.kestra.plugin.microsoft365.sharepoint` is created.  
2. It contains six tasks: `Create`, `Delete`, `Download`, `Export`, `List`, `Upload`.  
3. Authentication and required permission scopes are documented.  
4. End-to-end YAML examples are added to the plugin docs.  
5. Automated tests validate functionality for all tasks.  

### 🔗 References  
- Microsoft Graph SDK for Java: https://github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-java  
- SharePoint Graph API: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/sharepoint  
- OneDrive/SharePoint API for file access: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/onedrive  
- Kestra plugin developer guide: https://kestra.io/docs/plugin-developer-guide/trigger

issues.title: Add option to set default resync period at the operator level
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We've run into a problem with multiple operators running (1 per cluster up to ~20) against a single central HA Grafana instance, particularly managing alerts for each cluster. This number of operators with the default resync period of 10m means the alertmanager config in Grafana is being reloaded sometimes multiple times a minute. With the HA setup, this was meaning the config reloads were interfering with the unified alerting across replicas, meaning deduplication couldn't be done properly and we were running into duplicate and incorrectly grouped alerts. We can set a longer resync period (or disable it) on the individual alert CRs in the clusters, or there was the suggestion to update the CRD itself to the longer period. But this requires either some additional policies to ensure this is set on all alert CRs or having to manage our own CRD in step with the helm chart.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
What would be ideal is if we could set an environment var or flag on the operator. I.e. `--default-resync-period=24h`, potentially separated by resource (dashboards/alerts/etc) because this seems to be a particular problem with the alerting.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As mentioned above we can set it directly on the CRs, update the CRD ourselves or there was a suggestion if using GitOps to have a patch kustomization to update the resync period. We will likely use GitOps in the future but aren't currently so it's not an option for us and the other 2 are ongoing overhead that would be nice to avoid.

issues.title: Add a task that deletes the old data that has not been accessed in a while
issues.body:
A task for automatically deleting data in the memify pipeline that hasn't been accessed by retrievers for a specified period.

*NOTE: This issue is part of Contribute-to-Win. Please comment first to get assigned. Read the details [here](https://github.com/orgs/topoteretes/discussions/1361)*

## Overview

This task identifies and removes unused data (chunks, entities, summaries, associations) from the memify pipeline based on retrieval access patterns, helping maintain system efficiency and storage optimization.


## Usage

```python
from cognee.tasks.cleanup import cleanup_unused_data

# Preview cleanup (safe mode)
result = await cleanup_unused_data(days_threshold=30, dry_run=True)

# Execute cleanup
result = await cleanup_unused_data(days_threshold=30, dry_run=False)
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `days_threshold` | int | 30 | Days since last access to consider unused |
| `user_id` | UUID | None | Limit to specific user's data |

## What Gets Cleaned

- **Document Chunks**: Unused text segments
- **Entities**: Unaccessed extracted concepts  
- **Summaries**: Unused generated summaries
- **Associations**: Unused chunk relationships
- **Metadata**: Related database records

## Return Format

```python
{
    "status": "completed",  # or "dry_run"

issues.title: Add support for native `@supports` at-rule creation for feature queries
issues.body:
## Summary

Add native support for generating CSS `@supports` at-rules within the Styleframe TypeScript CSS API, allowing developers to use feature queries for progressive enhancement and browser compatibility.

## Motivation

Feature queries using the `@supports` at-rule enable conditional CSS based on browser support for specific features. This is important for writing robust, future-proof design systems code with Styleframe.

## Proposed Implementation

- Expose an API to define CSS feature queries using the native `@supports` at-rule.
- Ensure generated stylesheets include the correct feature query syntax and integrate with other Styleframe features.
- Add documentation and usage examples for the new API.

## References
- [MDN: CSS @supports](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@supports)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ability to create and compose feature queries using Styleframe.
- Type-safe API for feature query creation.
- Tests and documentation updated.

---

issues.title: Add support for native `@container` at-rule creation for container queries
issues.body:
## Summary

Add native support for generating CSS `@container` at-rules within the Styleframe TypeScript CSS API, enabling developers to use container queries for responsive design.

## Motivation

Container queries and the `@container` at-rule allow components to adapt their styles based on the size of their parent containers rather than the viewport. This is increasingly important for building flexible, composable design systems.

## Proposed Implementation

- Expose an API to define CSS container queries using the native `@container` at-rule.
- Ensure generated stylesheets include the correct container query syntax and integrate with other Styleframe features.
- Add documentation and usage examples for the new API.

## References
- [MDN: CSS @container](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@container)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ability to create and compose container queries using Styleframe.
- Type-safe API for container query creation.
- Tests and documentation updated.

issues.title: Add support for native `@layer` at-rule creation
issues.body:
## Summary

Add built-in support for generating native CSS `@layer` at-rules within the Styleframe TypeScript CSS API. This will enable users to structure their CSS with layers for improved specificity management and future compatibility.

## Motivation

CSS `@layer` is increasingly used for managing cascade and specificity. Supporting this natively will allow developers to leverage modern CSS features and organize their Design Systems code more effectively in Styleframe.

## Proposed Implementation

- Expose an API to define CSS layers using the native `@layer` at-rule.
- Ensure generated stylesheets include the correct layer syntax and can be composed with other Styleframe features.
- Add documentation and usage examples for the new API.

## References
- [MDN: CSS @layer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ability to create and compose CSS layers using Styleframe.
- Type-safe API for layer creation.
- Tests and documentation updated.
